sections.markdown:
## C — Winter, mountain, rural and work-zone driving; defensive driving basics

FACT_ID: sec11-F01 | anchor: A01
Snow and ice are at their most dangerous as they begin to melt, and slippery roads reduce tire grip and lengthen stopping distance. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec11-F02 | anchor: A01
Overpasses, bridges, shaded spots and snow-packed stretches can be icy even when the rest of the pavement is clear. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec11-F03 | anchor: A01
When traction is lost or a skid begins, lift off the gas and the brake together, then steer the front wheels toward your intended path. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec11-F04 | anchor: A01
Use extra care near snowplows clearing snow with flashing yellow lights; passing a government-operated plow working in tandem with other plows while its yellow lights flash is illegal. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec11-F05 | anchor: A01
Four-wheel drive improves traction but does not let a vehicle stop any sooner than an ordinary car. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec11-F06 | anchor: A01
Keep good tire tread; in winter, chains, snow tires or other traction devices are better and may be required on highways, though even these can slip on slick pavement. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec11-F07 | anchor: A01
Keep brakes in good repair and adjusted so every wheel brakes evenly. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec11-F08 | anchor: A01
With anti-lock brakes, if you begin to skid, ease off the gas, press the brake and steer the front wheels the way you want to go. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec11-F09 | anchor: A01
Without anti-lock brakes, use threshold braking when skidding or on slippery roads, pressing the brake to just short of locking the wheels. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec11-F10 | anchor: A01
Threshold braking works on cars with or without anti-lock brakes, but anti-lock braking technique cannot be used on a car without ABS. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec11-F11 | anchor: A01
Keep defrosters and wipers working, scrape off all ice, snow and frost even for a short trip, and clear inside fogging quickly by opening a window. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec11-F12 | anchor: A01
Snow plows and sanding trucks flash yellow and blue warning lights, so be extremely careful as you come up behind or go around them. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec11-F13 | anchor: A01
In snow and ice keep an extra large gap behind the vehicle ahead, slow down, and give pedestrians and bicyclists extra room to get around snow and ice. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec11-F14 | anchor: A01
Mountain driving brings steep grades, changing weather, bicyclists, wildlife and rocks on the road; shift to a lower gear to control speed going down steep grades. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec11-F15 | anchor: A01
Using the oncoming lane to pass is illegal near the crest of a hill, on a curve or anywhere your view of oncoming traffic is blocked. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec11-F16 | anchor: A01
In the mountains expect intersections hidden by trees, brush or crops, and animals on or beside the road. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec11-F17 | anchor: A01
If your vehicle struggles up a steep road, pull off at the first safe spot or keep right so others can pass; uphill vehicles have the right-of-way over downhill ones. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec11-F18 | anchor: A01
Rural highways are the most dangerous roads, with the highest U.S. death rate per mile driven of any road type. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec11-F19 | anchor: A01
Rural roads may have sharp or blind curves, steep hills and dips, poor or hidden guide signs, narrow lanes that make passing hard, and no shoulders or guard rails. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec11-F20 | anchor: A01
On rural roads expect blind driveways, T-intersections and side streets hidden by plants, plus rocks, debris, animals, crossing farm vehicles, unmarked railroad crossings and slow or small vehicles like bicycles. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec11-F21 | anchor: A01
Rural pavement is often rough or unpaved dirt and gravel with less traction, and washboarding on gravel roads can upset steering and control. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec11-F22 | anchor: A01
Potholes can make the vehicle bounce or jolt and cause the tires to lose traction. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec11-F23 | anchor: A01
Many bicyclist deaths happen on rural roads because of higher speeds, so slow down and give more than the required three feet when passing riders there, since dangerous wind blasts can lead to riders being struck. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec11-F24 | anchor: A02
Work zones contain equipment and workers and may change routes daily, and signs, cones and other devices placed ahead warn of the changes. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec11-F25 | anchor: A02
In a work zone stay alert, be ready to stop suddenly and never tailgate. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec11-F26 | anchor: A02
Large projects may use flaggers, portable concrete barriers, complex signs and reduced speed limits, and those lower limits give drivers more time to read and react. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec11-F27 | anchor: A02
Work-zone crews cannot be fully separated from traffic and must watch constantly for drivers who drift into the work area. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec11-F28 | anchor: A02
Police enforcement is often added in work zones, and fines are doubled there as they are in school zones. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec11-F29 | anchor: A02
In a work zone, obey work-zone speed signs and flaggers, and watch the vehicle ahead, because most work-zone crashes are rear-end collisions caused by inattention. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec11-F30 | anchor: A02
You cannot count on others obeying every rule, so drive calmly, ignore aggressive drivers and practice defensive driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec11-F31 | anchor: A02
Make sure every person in the vehicle wears a seat belt. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec11-F32 | anchor: A02
Colorado law bars using a mobile device while driving except to contact police or fire services, in an emergency, or with a hands-free accessory. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec11-F33 | anchor: A02
Colorado law bars texting while driving except to contact police or fire services or in an emergency; the listed texting exceptions do not include a hands-free accessory. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec11-F34 | anchor: A02
Keep both hands on the wheel at 8 and 4 or 9 and 3 o'clock, turn with the hand-over-hand or push-pull-slide method, and never palm the wheel or let it slide through your fingers after a turn. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec11-F35 | anchor: A02
Scan ahead, to the sides and behind, and always look left, right and left again when turning at, crossing or entering an intersection, watching for pedestrians, bicyclists and motorcyclists. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec11-F36 | anchor: A02
Look at least 10 seconds down the road, about one block in the city or half a mile on the open road, to avoid last-second braking or swerving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec11-F37 | anchor: A02
Check your rearview mirror every 5 to 8 seconds, more often in heavy traffic, and especially when changing lanes, slowing, backing, leaving an intersection or going down a long or steep hill. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec11-F38 | anchor: A02
Under normal conditions use the three-second rule: when the car ahead passes a fixed point, count three seconds, and if you reach the point first you are following too closely. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0021]
